scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A Guy In Trouble) for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. My girlfriend has a really sweet job with a lot of perks. She has flexible hours, can work from home, has a good benefits package, nice retirement plan, paid time off, and even gets to have nice office amenities like an espresso machine and fancy furniture. She's happy with her job and it's clear she's proud of what she's achieved. But I'm feeling frustrated because she talks about these perks a lot, especially around friends or at parties, and it seems like she's forgetting that not everyone has such a great job. I mentioned this to her, and she got defensive, saying I was jealous and that she worked hard to get where she is. She suggested I should focus on my own goals instead of complaining. I tried to explain that it's not just about her talking, but that she's always around people who don't have what she does, and maybe she could be a bit more modest. She stormed off, saying I'm the only one with a problem. Now, I'm wondering if I'm overreacting or if I'm justified in feeling this way. Let me think about both sides. On one hand, she's proud of her job and her achievements. It's natural to want to share that with others, especially when you're happy. She worked hard to get there, and it's important to acknowledge her efforts. Maybe I'm being too sensitive or jealous because I don't have the same kind of job, and that's making me uncomfortable. On the other hand, her constant talking about her perks might be coming off as bragging, especially in social settings where others might not have the same opportunities. It could make others feel uncomfortable or envious, which isn't great for social dynamics. Plus, it's making me feel bad because I'm comparing myself to her, and that's not healthy for our relationship. I also need to consider cultural and personal differences. Maybe she's just more outgoing and doesn't realize how her words are affecting me. Or perhaps she's not aware that her job is more privileged than most. It's possible that she doesn't see her job as extraordinary because it's her reality, so she doesn't realize others might not have the same experiences. I should also think about how to communicate my feelings without making her defensive. Maybe instead of telling her to stop bragging, I could express how her comments make me feel and suggest that she's around people who might not have the same opportunities. That way, it's about my feelings rather than her behavior, which might be easier for her to accept. Another angle is to reflect on whether I'm jealous. If I am, maybe I need to work on my own self-esteem or set personal goals to achieve something similar. That way, I can feel better about myself and not be envious of her success. In the end, I think it's a balance between respecting her achievements and being mindful of how her discussions affect others and our relationship. It's okay to want her to be more modest, but I also need to communicate that in a way that doesn't make her feel attacked or unappreciated.
